title: Mass dichotomy for two-valued functions
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i>0$ and $\sum_iw_i=1$. Suppose $\lambda>0$, $w_i\ge\lambda$ for every $i$, and $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ takes only the values $a$ and $b$, where $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\gamma=\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i$. Then either $f$ is identically $a$, $f$ is identically $b$, or $\lambda\le\gamma\le1-\lambda$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, and $0<\lambda\le w_i$ for every $i$. If $f:I\to\bbr$ takes values in $\{a,b\}$, then either $f$ is identically $a$, or identically $b$, or $\lambda\le\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i\le1-\lambda$.
